claim: Exact sparse named-field memory needs at least log2 choose(n,k)+kb bits under distinguishability and no external memory.
limitation: Not a novel theorem; hindsight relevance does not imply online identifiability.

claim: Sequential memory must respect when X, S, and J become available.
limitation: The finite model explicitly leaves S and J public at their specified stages.

claim: The isolated first and second cut errors in the four-bit example are 3/16 and 1/4.
limitation: Uniform independent source and specified query distributions only.

claim: Attaining the child-optimal 1/4 error requires at least eight parent states and three bits suffice.
limitation: Checked restricted example; no novelty certification or general scaling result.

claim: The two-bit-then-one-bit chain has error at least 49/192.
limitation: This is a conservative lower bound; the exact chain optimum was not computed.

claim: The record diagnostic has 810 configurations and favors sound retirement over plain LRU in its constructed setting.
limitation: No LLMs; explicit retirement signals; configurations are not independent benchmark samples.

claim: Visible history edits can also alter provider-managed reasoning state.
limitation: Model and API specific; recheck current continuity requirements before experiments.

claim: Shorter prompts do not by themselves establish lower total-run cost.
limitation: Cache behavior, future reuse, manager calls, retrieval, and retries affect the result.

claim: Native compaction, structured retention, and compatible masking are necessary comparison candidates.
limitation: Their relative performance has not been evaluated by this project.

claim: A structural compatibility theorem or a reproducible practical improvement would be the candidate contribution.
